vulnerabilities.title: Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification) via the `parseMember` function in the baggage parser. When Baggage propagation is enabled and extraction processes attacker-controlled headers before authentication or on a public route, an attacker can send a valid near-limit W3C baggage header with thousands of short properties; parsing eagerly materializes and copies property objects, causing disproportionate bounded allocations that increase memory use and garbage-collection pressure under repeated or concurrent requests.

**Notes**

- At the parsing step, input size bounds the amplification: v1.46.0 and v1.47.0-rc.1 enforce an 8,192-byte raw-input limit and a 64-member limit; earlier releases use a 4,096-byte per-member limit, so the 8,191-byte example does not apply across the full affected range.

**Workarounds**

- Place authentication middleware before `otelhttp` extraction so unauthenticated requests are rejected before attacker-controlled baggage is parsed.
## Remediation
Upgrade `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage` to version 1.47.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-rrfc-gjm9-cgrj)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/f09d1de32f4ac7e5ef16394533721106b1a57b89)
- [GitHub PR](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/9024)
